answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before receiving a daily job quota, whether the task is sourcing velvet, pricing saffron, or composing a sonnet. Creating more identities grants more quotas only if each new identity posts another bond. An attacker running 1,000 identities must therefore immobilize $100,000 for a month, making mass account creation costly even when generating names and keys is free.
